claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy.
The HVAF-i7 feedstock particle-size range is 15–45 μm.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces coatings of acceptable quality.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces insufficient coating thickness.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase in-flight particle velocity.
A longer spray distance provides more residence time for particles to accelerate in the gas stream.
The resulting higher particle velocity increases kinetic impact at the substrate.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy improves particle flattening upon impact.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy improves cohesion and inter-particle bonding.
Stronger particle impingement reduces particle rebound.
Reduced rebound and improved impact behavior increase deposition efficiency.
Increasing the spray distance to 300–350 mm will produce a thicker coating than the baseline process.
The thicker coating will retain high-quality adhesion.
The longer spray distance will retain low as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention can be applied under ambient deposition conditions within internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The resulting coating should remain suitable for high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
Spray distances outside the 300–350 mm range or changes in torch configuration may negate the benefit.

contradictions.description: A 300–350 mm torch-to-substrate spray distance is geometrically incompatible with deposition on the interior wall of a 120 mm-diameter cavity as written, because the available radial span is at most 120 mm and normally about 60 mm from the centerline. No axial or angled torch arrangement is specified that would reconcile these conditions.
